name: Psychology
description: Illusions, phobias and the strange things brains do.
theme: the human brain and the odd things it does: illusions and phobias, memory slips, sleep and dreams, the biases everyone falls for, and the surprising facts about the organ doing the thinking
angles: a number about the brain people can picture, what it weighs, what share of the body's energy it burns, how long a thought takes
what a specific fear is called, from the common ones to the absurdly precise
the everyday feeling that turns out to have a proper name, the earworm, the tip of the tongue, the jolt as you fall asleep
something the brain flatly refuses to do, tickle itself, see its own blind spot, stay awake past a point
a famous illusion, and what it makes people see that is not there
a bias everyone at the table has, described until they recognise themselves, name it
senses that behave unlike all the others
the part of the body holding far more nerve cells than anyone expects
sleep oddities, which stage dreams live in, how fast people fall asleep, what sleepwalkers can do
a classic experiment told as the story of what actually happened in the room
the way memory fails, and the name for that particular failure
an animal whose brain beats ours at one specific thing
a strange effect traced to one named region of the brain
how long something takes, to form a habit, to forget a dream, to recognise a face
a word borrowed from psychology into everyday speech, and what it properly means
avoid: clinical diagnosis and mental health advice, findings that failed to replicate or are now disputed, pop-psychology myths like left brain versus right brain and learning styles, brain training and self improvement claims, precise percentages that vary from one source to the next, and any question whose true answer is an explanation rather than a name, a number or a body part
